                                              Re: Skeptics Debunkers And Believers
  From: Franklin D. Fields <fields.nul>
  Date: Fri, 31 Oct 2008 10:34:04 -0400 (EDT)
  Archived: Sat, 01 Nov 2008 08:00:28 -0400
  Subject: Re: Skeptics Debunkers And Believers

  >Source: AboutSeti.Com - Carlsbad, New Mexico
  >http://www.aboutseti.com/blog/skeptics-debunkers-and-believers
  >Thursday, October 30, 2008
  >Skeptics, Debunkers And Believers
  >by Mac Tonnies
  >Followers of the search for extraterrestrial intelligence --
  >whether 'mainstream' exobiology or the marginal exploits of
  >'ufology' - are routinely confronted with three terms that
  >quietly challenge assumptions of reality: "skeptic", "debunker"
  >and "believer". In the storm of claims, hypotheses and
  >accusations that define esoteric research, these labels are
  >routinely misused. I'd like to take this opportunity to look a
  >bit closer at these emotionally charged words in order to see
  >what they really mean, and how they sculpt the epistemological
  >landscape. (I suspect that most readers versed in 'forbidden
  >science' secretly know all of this already, but the public arena
  >incessantly distorts definitions to suit its own politics;
  >consequently, one rarely sees 'skeptic', 'debunker' or
  >'believer' used in proper context.)
  >1.) Skeptics
  >Skeptics are thinkers. Skeptics neither debunk nor believe -
  >unless they are able to establish that a given phenomenon
  >deserves to be debunked. 'Belief' is not a luxury the true
  >skeptic can afford; the mechanics of skeptical thought are
  >rooted in probability and open-mindedness. Being a skeptic
  >requires courage and intellectual flexibility. What looks like a
  >neat idea may turn out to be unsubstantiated nonsense;
  >conversely, it might be the real thing.
  >2.) Debunkers
  >Debunkers comprise the most virulent of contemporary self-
  >described "skeptics". There is nothing inherently unsound about
  >debunking, contrary to the many appeals on behalf of the 'pro'
  >side of any given paranormal controversy. But in order to
  >debunk, the subject being debunked must be bunk.
  >The term 'debunker' is often taken as a negative word, perhaps
  >best personified by orangutan scientist-theologian Dr. Zaius in
  >Planet Of The Apes. But there's nothing wrong with being a
  >debunker as long as the debunker can back up his or her claims.
  >Of course, this doesn't mean that some commentators won't abuse
  >the urge to debunk - usually in the name of 'skepticism'. For
  >example, astronomer Donald Menzel 'debunked' countless UFO
  >sightings based on his scientifically baseless conviction that
  >there could be no such thing as an alien craft in Earth's
  >airspace. Veteran ufologist Philip Klass continued in Menzel's
  >role, correctly debunking many spurious UFO reports but
  >erroneously 'debunking' others. This is inevitable, as Klass'
  >self-stated maxim was that all UFO reports can be attributed to
  >prosaic causes.
  >3.) Believers


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/nov/m01-001.shtml[12/12/2011 09:35:18]
Re: Skeptics Debunkers And Believers


  >Along with faux-debunkers, believers are the most significant
  >fetter to open-minded inquiry. Believers have no pressing need
  >for facts; a few vague correlations or anonymous 'insider'
  >remarks will suffice. Believers typically revolve around the
  >notion that great shifts in scientific thought are usually
  >initiated by lone eccentrics whose genius is often recognized
  >only posthumously. Thus, their being branded as "cranks" by the
  >mainstream is flaunted as a badge of honor, as if identifying
  >them as architects of the Next Great Paradigm.
  >While genuine pioneers are indeed often derided in their time,
  >this is no promise that today's 'crackpot' theory will be
  >vindicated. However, this doesn't faze believers. Nothing fazes
  >believers. True believers will weave contradictory evidence into
  >their own models of reality, rationalizing it with arcane
  >philosophical acrobatics. (Try wrapping your mind around the
  >schizophrenic cosmos conceived by Christian Fundamentalists and
  >'Creation Scientists'.)
  >We should all strive to be skeptics. But that means taking a
  >hard look at the principles of skepticism as relayed by the
  >mainstream skeptical community (whose output is as flawed by
  >what it doesn't present as believer-oriented media is flawed by
  >its credulity).
  I would add at least three more terms.
  Experiencers - Those that have experienced a UFO or ET and know
  first hand the phenomena is real.
  Understanders -- Those that were skeptics but through careful
  research have concluded that the phenomena is real.
  Debunker Operators - This category may correctly be a sub-
  category under Debunker. These are the people that are either
  Experiencers or Understanders but for some reason work to keep
  the true reality of the phenomena secret by purposefully
  manipulating data or using other means to deceive the public.
  Frank

  Listen to 'Strange Days... Indeed' - The PodCast

                                   Strange Object Photographed Over Parque Urquiza
  From: Scott Corrales <lornis1.nul>
  Date: Fri, 31 Oct 2008 11:09:00 -0400 (GMT-04:00)
  Archived: Sat, 01 Nov 2008 08:03:54 -0400
  Subject: Strange Object Photographed Over Parque Urquiza

  Source: Compacto de Noticias
  http://www.compactodenoticias.com.ar/
  Date: October 31, 2008
  Argentina: Strange Object Photographed over Parque Urquiza,
  Parana=A1
  A resident of Parana=A1 photographed his daugter near Danza de la
  Flecha. Imagine his surprise when upon enlarging the
  photo, he saw a strange object in it. Sources from the Oro Verde
  Observatory say that they will look into the case.
  Only days ago, Miguel Angel Osuna went to Parana=A1's Parque
  Urquiza to take a picture of his daughter, who will be turning
  15, in order use the mural as an image upon which party guests
  can leave their signatures and best wishes for the birthday
  girl.
  The family chose the rock quarries located near Danza de la
  Flecha as a background, using the modern architecture of the
  Maran Suites & Towers Hotel as a backdrop.
  They were astonished to learn, upon enlarging the image at a
  photo shop, that they had taken a picture of an unidentified
  flying object (UFO). In the image's background, to the right, it
  is possible to see a small point that raises suspicions upon
  being enlarged.
  In an interview with Elonce TV, Osuna said that "the fellow [at
  the photo shop] told us there was a strange object in the
  photograph that was neither a helicopter nor an airplane." The
  photo was taken on October 21 around 17:00 hours.
  Osuna used a digital camera and his father a professional one;
  the UFO appears in the photograph taken with the first device.
  When consulted, Mariano Peter, with the Oro Grande Observatory,
  pointed out that "whenever strange things are seen in the sky,
  people ask us. We haven't received any queries up to now."
  Nonetheless, he stated that the original image should be
  analyzed to ascertain that it was indeed a physical object, and
  its type. In this regard, he noted that if anyone saw something
  unusual on the date that the photo was taken, they should
  approach the observatory to discuss it.

                                             Argentine Witness Suffers Facial Paralysis
  From: Scott Corrales <lornis1.nul>
  Date: Fri, 31 Oct 2008 11:09:34 -0400 (GMT-04:00)
  Archived: Sat, 01 Nov 2008 08:07:50 -0400
  Subject: Argentine Witness Suffers Facial Paralysis

  Source: Diario El Dia
  http://www.eldia.com.ar/edis/20081029/2008102922220.htm
  Date: October 29, 2008
  Argentina: La Rioja UFO Witness Suffers Facial Paralysis
  Man reports seeing three UFOs in La Rioja and experienced facial
  paralysis; says that event "changed his life" affecting him not
  only psychologically but also physically.
  Witness claims seeing three UFOs over the locality of Villa
  Castelli; experience left him with "facial paralysis".
  Fernando Guerrero, who was intensely sought after by news media
  throughout Argentina, stated on radio that he has been feeling
  "very strange" since he saw the strange phenomenon.
  The event took place on Saturday, October 25, when Guerrero, who
  drives the only ambulance owned by that community of La Rioja,
  reached his place of work in fear and told his co-workers what
  he had seen.
  As he drove the ambulance from Villa Union toward neighboring
  Villa Castelli, he became aware of a significant increase in the
  light coming from the cell phone he was using at the moment.
  "It's going to burn up." That was the first thought that crossed
  his mind, adding that the CD he was listening to at the time
  "suddenly stopped, and a loud squealing sound could be heard."
  At that moment three objects moved along in the sky. The
  privileged witness did not doubt to use his cellphone to capture
  the image.
  "I immediately used my phone to take a picture of them, it was
  lovely, a real spectacle," the driver told his co-workers, who
  ultimately chose to report it to the local print media.
  Now, Guerrero decided to speak to the press for the first time,
  insisting over and over that he feels "different" and explains
  that since the dramatic close encounter, half of his face is
  numb, exactly in the parietal region where he was struck by the
  "powerful light" by the Unidentified Flying Object.
  "The part of my head that was exposed to the light when the UFO
  appeared now feels numb and hot," said the man, who refused to
  say if he received phone calls from scientists and researchers.
  It emerged that researchers had tried to get in touch with the
  witness to the phenomenon to glean details of the sightings as
  part of the search for new eyewitness accounts for UFO events in
  this region.
  The two latest cases occurred on April 14 and 15, when tourists
  visiting Quebrada del Condor in Tupungato, Mendoza, and
  residents of the Riojan department of Arauco, respectively,
  claimed seeing strange objects in the sky.

  From: Scott Corrales <lornis1.nul>
  Date: Fri, 31 Oct 2008 11:10:57 -0400 (GMT-04:00)
  Archived: Sat, 01 Nov 2008 08:12:14 -0400
  Subject: UFO Over Tamaulipas Mexico

  Source: www.analuisacid.com
  Date: October 30, 2008
  Mexico: UFOs Over Tamaulipas
  By Ana Luisa Cid
  Since October 22, 2008 to date there have been numerous UFO
  sighting reports emerging from the Mexican state of Tamaulipas.
  The most significant of these are the ones recorded in Ciudad
  Madero, Tampico and Rio Bravo.
  The state's Direccion de Proteccion Civil (Civil Defense) has
  received phone calls from witnesses hat are now exceed 50
  reports.
  The Hechos news program on Television Azteca made the first
  images known, corresponding to a video recorded by Mrs. Liliana
  Vazquez
  According to the news report, on October 24, 2008, during a
  ceremony conmemorating United Nations Day , students and
  teachers of the Venustiano Carranza school in Tampico saw three
  white spheres in the sky. They argued over whether they were
  balloons or UFOs, although one student said that the objects
  resembled =E2=80=9Ctwo joined plates=E2=80=9D. Parents were also present
  during the event, and it was one of them =E2=80=93 Mrs. Vazquez =E2=80=93
  who videotaped the event.
  The same newscast reported that it would conduct an
  investigation to find out if a private company had launched
  helium balloons that morning.
  Moreover, Mr. Jose Alonso Galicia Fabela, a resident of Rio
  Bravo, documented the transti of a sphere that appeared to be on
  a helicopter's flight path. This recording is dated October 27,
  13:30 hours.
  The witness says that he was following the helicopter with his
  camcorder when he suddenly saw the spherical object, which moved
  from south to north.
  While both videos appear to show the same thing, it should be
  noted that the cities where they were recorded are quite distant
  from each other. Rio Bravo is in northeastern Tamaulipas, while
  Tampico is toward the southeast.

  Needles UFO Crash Update
  CBS News investigative reporter George Knapp will present this
  year's UFO Crash Conference Keynote Speech about the May 14,
  2008 Needles, CA UFO Crash and subsequent Military Retrieval.
  New information will be disclosed. Register today and secure
  your chance to hear about this highly credible UFO crash event.
  Join us Saturday, November 8th at the Tuscany Suites & Casino
  where George Knapp will be the keynote speaker at our annual UFO
  Conference Banquet Dinner.
  On May 14, 2008, a large cylindrical, glowing object streaked
  out of the sky and fell to the earth just south of Needles
  California. It landed with a loud thump in impenetrable thickets
  of salt cedar just west of the Colorado River. Within minutes, a
  phalanx of helicopters arrived at the scene, including a large
  sky crane. The still-glowing object was lifted into the air and
  flown away to an unknown location. Hours later, residents of
  Needles and the surrounding area reported seeing unusual
  vehicles sporting government license plates and blacked out
  windows, manned by personnel in civilian clothing but with
  military bearings.
  Several eyewitnesses saw the object and report while it was in
  the sky and say it appeared to slow down, then accelerate during
  its descent. The witness closest to the impact point, a
  fisherman known as "Bob on the River", reported his sighting to
  a local radio station but then vanished. Residents of the area
  reported intrusions by strange men in strange vehicles, some of
  whom asked penetrating questions about the UFO and about the key
  witnesses.
  Investigative reporter George Knapp has located and questioned
  more than a dozen eyewitnesses, including Bob on the River and
  has pinpointed the area where the object crashed. In addition,
  he tracked down the suspected Men In Black described by Needles
  residents and confirmed these personnel do work for a highly-
   secretive national security agency whose existence is not
  widely known.
  This presentation will examine the relevant eyewitness
  testimony, will transport the audience to the approximate
  location of the crash, and will examine possible explanations
  for what kind of object fell from the sky. It will also reveal
  the existence of the classified operation underway in that area.
  Included in the presentation will be several video clips, news
  reports, and interview segments.

                                                              'Magnetic Portals'
   From: Martin Shough <parcellular.nul>
   Date: Sun, 2 Nov 2008 19:03:49 -0000
   Archived: Mon, 03 Nov 2008 20:55:39 -0500
   Subject: 'Magnetic Portals'

   Portals in the sky are now scientific. It's official. NASA says
   so ;-)
   An interesting story which is being widely discussed on the net.
   http://science.nasa.gov/headlines/y2008/30oct_ftes.htm
   [Begin Quote]
   Magnetic Portals Connect Sun and Earth
   During the time it takes you to read this article, something will
   happen high overhead that until recently many scientists didn't
   believe in. A magnetic portal will open, linking Earth to the sun
   93 million miles away. Tons of high-energy particles may flow
   through the opening before it closes again, around the time you
   reach the end of the page.
   "It's called a flux transfer event or 'FTE,'" says space
   physicist David Sibeck of the Goddard Space Flight Center. "Ten
   years ago I was pretty sure they didn't exist, but now the
   evidence is incontrovertible."
   Indeed, today Sibeck is telling an international assembly of
   space physicists at the 2008 Plasma Workshop in Huntsville,
   Alabama, that FTEs are not just common, but possibly twice as
   common as anyone had ever imagined.
   Researchers have long known that the Earth and sun must be
   connected. Earth's magnetosphere (the magnetic bubble that
   surrounds our planet) is filled with particles from the sun that
   arrive via the solar wind and penetrate the planet's magnetic
   defenses. They enter by following magnetic field lines that can
   be traced from terra firma all the way back to the sun's
   atmosphere.
   "We used to think the connection was permanent and that solar
   wind could trickle into the near-Earth environment anytime the
   wind was active," says Sibeck. "We were wrong. The connections
   are not steady at all. They are often brief, bursty and very
   dynamic."
   Several speakers at the Workshop have outlined how FTEs form: On
   the dayside of Earth (the side closest to the sun), Earth's
   magnetic field presses against the sun's magnetic field.
   Approximately every eight minutes, the two fields briefly merge
   or "reconnect," forming a portal through which particles can
   flow. The portal takes the form of a magnetic cylinder about as
   wide as Earth. The European Space Agency's fleet of four Cluster
   spacecraft and NASA's five THEMIS probes have flown through and
   surrounded these cylinders, measuring their dimensions and
   sensing the particles that shoot through. "They're real," says
   Sibeck.
   Now that Cluster and THEMIS have directly sampled FTEs, theorists
   can use those measurements to simulate FTEs in their computers
   and predict how they might behave. Space physicist Jimmy Raeder
   of the University of New Hampshire presented one such simulation
   at the Workshop. He told his colleagues that the cylindrical


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/nov/m03-003.shtml[12/12/2011 09:35:30]
'Magnetic Portals'

   portals tend to form above Earth's equator and then roll over
   Earth's winter pole. In December, FTEs roll over the north pole;
   in July they roll over the south pole.....
   There are many unanswered questions: Why do the portals form
   every 8 minutes? How do magnetic fields inside the cylinder twist
   and coil? "We're doing some heavy thinking about this at the
   Workshop," says Sibeck.
   Meanwhile, high above your head, a new portal is opening,
   connecting your planet to the sun.
   [End Quote]
   ----
   A discussion relating this to so-called "electric universe" ideas
   here
   http://tinyurl.com/64fz7h
   is also quite interesting, suggesting that the so-called
   "magnetic portals" should be better thought of in terms of what
   must *cause* magnetic field, i.e.an elctric current flowing
   between sun and earth, and that earth's ionosphere and surface -
    separated by an insulating atmosphere - behaves like a leaky
   capacitor that regularly charges up from the sun and breaks down.
   They make the connection to phenomena like sprites and elves,
   poorly understood plasma phenomena occurring high in the
   atmosphere.
   Much more here about NASA's CLUSTER "magnetic reconnection" data
   and the above ideas:
   http://thunderbolts.info/thunderblogs/mgmirkin.htm
   It's fun to speculate that such processes could also be related
   to certain types of UAPs in the lower troposphere that might give
   rise to UFO reports. No doubt the CONDIGN author would have added
   a section on it had he been writing today. It would certainly be
   interesting if those periodicities (8-minute* and seasonal) could
   be discovered in some class of UAP observations, although I admit
   it's a very long shot.
   Just another area to keep an eye on perhaps? It's certainly more
   evidence that we really don't understand earth's electromagnetic
   environment half as well as we think.

   Martin Shough
   *BTW, the sun-earth light travel time of ~8 mins seems too close
   to be coincidence.

  Subject: The Triumph Of Ostriches



  Source: Billy Cox's Blog De Void - Sarasota, Florida, USA
  http://tinyurl.com/6bwq5d
  Friday, October 31, 2008

  The Triumph Of Ostriches
  By Billy Cox
  Published: Friday, October 31, 2008 at 12:57 p.m.
  Last Modified: Friday, October 31, 2008 at 1:04 p.m.
  What a difference 55 years makes, ay?
  UFOs evidently continue to troll the skies near Stephenville,
  Tex., people on the ground continue to see them and even take
  photos, and jet fighters continue to keep a wary tab on events:
  see:
  http://tinyurl.com/5tsh86
  And the military continues to maintain its rigid silence because
  to do otherwise would be an admission that we've blown hundreds
  of billions of dollars on a leaky roof.
  But once upon a time, back before the Pentagon knew how hopeless
  its situation really was, the Air Force actually encouraged
  Americans to help collect UFO data. Check out David Duncan's
  little gem at:
  http://www.thekeyhoereport.com/uncategorized/retro-ufology-from-1953
  It's a 1953 Popular Science article detailing how the USAF
  distributed 35mm cameras to "detectives on the trail of the
  flying saucers". If that seems a little exotic, remember that in
  1952, UFOs weren't just buzzing the capitol, the Pentagon was
  holding press conferences about it and telling Americans not to
  freak.
  Anyhow, fitted with special diffraction grating plates, these
  Videon Stereo cameras were designed to bend light in a way that
  would identify their source as a solid or a gas. But writer Ralph
  Steiner assured readers who wanted to photograph UFOs that custom
  cameras weren't necessary.
  "Any stereo camera will do." he wrote. "In fact, when I phoned
  the Pentagon to inquire whether the Air Force would be interested
  in photos taken with single-lens cameras, I was assured that any
  shot of a flying saucer made through a diffraction grating - even
  with a box Brownie - would be more than welcome".
  Steiner included beaucoup photo tips and a USAF address for
  sending undeveloped film. Can you imagine the military soliciting
  the public for that sort of evidence today?


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/nov/m05-004.shtml[12/12/2011 09:35:32]
The Triumph Of Ostriches


  "Uh, folks, we're really having trouble keeping UFOs out of
  restricted airspace over President Bush's ranch in Crawford
  lately, so we'd like you to try to photograph the suckers with
  these special cameras so we can take the evidence to Congress and
  lobby for countermeasure funding in a more open and accountable
  fashion".
  The same month the Popular Science piece ran, the CIA secretly
  convened a panel of scientists - later known as the Robertson
  Committee - to figure out how to manage the UFO problem. The
  consensus was to sweep the subject off the front pages by
  debunking the phenomenon. See:
  http://www.cufos.org/IUR_article3.html
  It's one of the Agency's few legacies where the cliche
  successfully applies today: Mission Accomplished.

UFO Believers Choose Silence Over Skepticism




                                                          UFO Updates
                                   A mailing list for the study of UFO-related phenomena
                                               'Its All Here In Black & White'
    Location: UFOUpDatesList.Com > 2008 > Nov > Nov 5

                                       UFO Believers Choose Silence Over Skepticism
  From: UFO UpDates - Toronto <ufoupdates.nul>
  Date: Wed, 05 Nov 2008 10:00:00 -0500
  Archived: Wed, 05 Nov 2008 10:00:00 -0500
  Subject: UFO Believers Choose Silence Over Skepticism



  Source: The Columbian, Vancouver, Washington, USA
  http://www.individual.com/story.php?story=91153832
  Nov 03, 2008

  UFO Believers Choose Silence Over Skepticism: Meeting In Battle
  Ground Aimed At Sharing Stories Of Sightings
  Scott Hewitt
  360-735-4529
  or
  scott.hewitt.nul

  Battle Ground--When it comes to unidentified flying objects,
  there are more questions than answers. And there's more silence
  than sharing.
  The 30 or so people who turned out at Rocky's Pizza on Saturday
  to share UFO stories said talking about their experiences was
  something of a novelty - since confessing such things tends to
  result in skeptical stares and unflattering judgments about their
  sanity.
  "I don't really talk about it. People aren't going to believe
  it," said one woman who had driven away from a Dairy Queen in
  Utah in the mid-1970s with a couple of friends when a bright
  light came to rest directly over their car.
  "We better not tell anybody," another man remembered deciding
  with a friend after they saw zigzagging white lights in the sky.
  "They wouldn't believe us anyway."
  Joy French of Coeur d'Alene, Idaho, convened the meeting. She's
  been on a swing through the Pacific Northwest to locate fellow
  UFO believers.
  She wasn't disappointed - there was plenty of belief in the
  room, if not too much hard information.
  Many said they'd seen impossibly fast-moving, utterly silent
  lights, or saucer-shaped craft zooming in formation, or
  mysterious orange balls. Nobody had an explanation - and nobody
  had a tale to equal French's.
  In the early 1980s, she said, she was staying near Lake Merwin
  and driving downhill to visit a friend when suddenly she
  discovered it was her friend driving, not her. She couldn't
  remember what had happened.
  Then there was a bright flash of light and the car stopped dead.
  Her friend went out to open the hood and determined there was
  nothing wrong with the car.
  Another memory blank. The next day, French and her friend got


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/nov/m05-005.shtml[12/12/2011 09:35:32]
UFO Believers Choose Silence Over Skepticism

  together - and each confessed to believing they'd been abducted
  by a UFO.
  "We made a pact we'd never talk about it," she said.
  But these days French, 84, has changed her mind. She believes the
  U.S. government knows more than it's telling about UFO visits,
  and the way to make it fess up is to start talking. If you tell
  what happened to you, she said, you just might find your neighbor
  has been sitting on a similarly strange experience.
  French believes she was taken aboard a UFO - but "they probably
  threw me back because I had a complete hysterectomy, so I'm no
  use to them."
  "I want to get hypnotized one of these days," she said, to dig
  out exactly what did happen to her. She would have done it
  Saturday before the group, she said, but she wasn't feeling well
  enough.
  Why is the government hiding the truth about UFOs? Because it
  wants to keep the advanced technology it took from crashed alien
  spacecraft to itself - to retain the upper hand.
  That's one theory, anyway. Many other theories were discussed,
  including these: Extraterrestrials are visitors from the future,
  or from another galaxy, or another dimension. Some think they're
  benevolent overseers who're making sure we don't destroy
  ourselves. Others think we're just a science experiment set in
  motion by curious alien youngsters.
  And a couple believers described cosmic vibrations, mystery
  voices, flying pyramids and golden light that healed what ailed
  them.
  "I'm not scared of them. I don't think they're here to hurt us,"
  French said. "I think they're here to rescue us because we are
  destroying our planet."
  French and her audience cited The History Channel and other
  television fare as the primary source of their theories.
  Still, it's hard to completely dismiss all UFO stories. Twice
  this year - once in January and once late last month - there
  were flurries of sightings in Texas. Also last month, the British
  defense ministry released thousands of documents about UFO
  reports.
  The United States Air Force investigated more than 12,000 UFO
  sightings between 1952 and 1969, and concluded that the vast
  majority were misidentified aircraft or atmospheric or space
  phenomena.
  UFO believers, of course, are skeptical about that.

  Jarring Revival Of Interest In UFOs
  The Southern Beat By Rolly Espina
  Recently, I found myself stupefied by a series of television
  footages of sightings of unidentified flying objects (UFOs). But
  I thought it was just a revival of a fad and dismissed them as an
  obsession by a group of dedicated believers in extra-
  terrestrials.
  But it seems that is not the case. I was jarred recently by a
  letter received from a long-lost godson, Edwin Gatia, an amateur
  astronomer who is now living in Philadelphia City in the United
  States.
  The letter struck me because Gatia, whom I have not seen for
  decades, suddenly recalled to me the story that I had written in
  the Iwag, the provincial newsletter during martial law in Negros
  Occidental.
  That was 30 years ago. But Gatia was insistent on asking for more
  details on that alleged “landing” in the Talisay City area by a
  UFO which was witnessed by several people in a small village
  beside the First Farmers Milling Co.
  And he also mentioned about having interviewed my late father,
  Sir Knight Fulgencio R. Espina, on another UFO spotting which the
  latter had erringly described to me.
  I would have dismissed that request for additional information
  had not Gatia told me that he was gathering additional data on a
  possible book project “Unidentified and Unknown: The Philippine
  UFO Experience” he is preparing to publish before the
  International UFO Congress in Nevada in February next year.
  “The book covers other sightings reported in the country that
  date back to the late 40s and the early 50s as well as the recent
  ones reported in the 1980s,” Gatia said.
  Well, for one, although I had forgotten about that incident, I
  remember that the US Enquirer Magazine sent down to Bacolod a
  writer who stayed for sometime in the area taking photos and
  interviewing alleged witnesses.
  I also know that (ret.) Col. Patricio Lomongo was the then PC
  provincial commander. He had ordered the incident investigated,
  although I did not hear about the findings by the investigators
  nor did I get a copy of that report.
  Incidentally, Gatia told me that he had interviewed my father
  whose sighting report was provided as Case No. “MRS”: 9790s418; N


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/nov/m06-001.shtml[12/12/2011 09:35:34]
Jarring Revival Of Interest In UFOs

  1055N12320E Fabrica, Negros del Norte.”
  In short, there are a lot of serious people in the world whose
  focus remain targeted on the UFOs. And that international
  conference in Nevada, USA, is expected to renew keen interest in
  this unexplained sightings which, just today, remain unsolved or
  cloaked in controversies.
  At least, Gatia is one person who is convinced that there must be
  something to it. Unfortunately, I have always believed that he is
  a serious astronomy student and must have reasons for his
  dedicated focus on UFO.

                                                 Fate Magazine 60 Years 400 Issues
  From: UFO UpDates - Toronto <ufoupdates.nul>
  Date: Thu, 06 Nov 2008 07:07:12 -0500
  Archived: Thu, 06 Nov 2008 07:07:12 -0500
  Subject: Fate Magazine 60 Years 400 Issues



  Source: Fate Magazine - Lakeville Minnesota
  www.fatemag.com
  September-October 2008
  Magazine Commemorates Noteworthy Milestone
  FATE celebrates 60 years of covering the strange and unknown
  (Lakeville MN) - Six decades before the History Channel's
  Monster Quest, A&E's Paranormal State, late-night radio's Coast
  to Coast AM, and countless websites, blogs, books, and movies
  began captivating audiences with true tales of the paranormal -
   there was FATE - a first-of-its-kind publication dedicated to
  in-depth coverage of mysterious and unexplained phenomena. FATE
  was a true journalistic pioneer, covering issues like electronic
  voice phenomena, cattle mutilations, life on Mars, telepathic
  communication with animals, and UFOs at a time when discussing
  such things was neither hip nor trendy like it is today. This
  month, FATE celebrates the 60th anniversary of its founding and
  the publication of its 700th issue, a rare feat of longevity
  achieved by only a select few U.S. periodicals.
  The year was 1948. President Harry Truman was in a tight race for
  reelection with Thomas Dewey. New nations emerged in Asia,
  Africa, and the Middle East. Ex-GIs moved their growing families
  into new American suburbs. The Cold War was in its infancy, and
  the Space Age was still a dream=85but across the nation and around
  the world, people observed strange objects flying through the
  skies.
  Two Chicago-based magazine editors, Raymond A. Palmer and Curtis
  B. Fuller, took a close look at the public's fascination with
  flying saucers and saw the opportunity of a lifetime.With help
  from connections in the worlds of science fiction and alternative
  spirituality, they launched a new magazine dedicated to the
  objective exploration of the world's mysteries. They gave their
  "cosmic reporter" the name FATE.
  FATE's first issue, published in Spring 1948, featured as its
  cover story the first-hand report of pilot Kenneth Arnold on his
  UFO sighting of the previous year, an event widely recognized by
  UFO historians as the birth of the modern UFO era.
  Other topics covered in this and subsequent issues included
  vanished civilizations, communication with spirits,
  synchronicity, exotic religions, monsters and giants, outof-
   place artifacts, and phenomena too bizarre for categorization.
  This mix of subjects set a template that the magazine would
  follow for six decades and counting. In many ways, FATE magazine
  created the genre that is now known as "the paranormal".
  Palmer and Fuller's judgment of FATE's potential proved correct,
  and as demand for the magazine grew its publication frequency
  increased quickly from quarterly to bimonthly to monthly. Palmer
  sold his share of the magazine in the late 1950s, and Fuller


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/nov/m06-003.shtml[12/12/2011 09:35:35]
Fate Magazine 60 Years 400 Issues

  brought his wife Mary aboard to help run the growing business.
  FATE's success spawned scores of imitators over the years, but
  none lasted very long. Through the decades FATE kept going,
  doggedly promoting the validity of paranormal studies but
  unafraid to reveal major events as hoaxes or frauds when it was
  warranted. Among the famous cases debunked by FATE were the
  Philadelphia Experiment and the Amityville Horror.
  So how does FATE still stay relevant after all this time?
  Especially in a fast-paced, high-tech world that is often short
  on attention span and long on cynicism, how does a magazine like
  FATE continue to thrive? Editor-in-Chief Phyllis Galde says,
  "FATE allows readers to think for themselves by providing them
  with stories that mainstream publications don't dare touch. The
  truth is, reality does not conform to the neat and tidy box that
  many people would like to wedge it into. Our world is a bizarre
  and wondrous place and our universe is filled with mystery - it
  is teeming with the unknown. People are longing for something
  more than the mundane transactions of everyday existence. FATE
  feeds the soul's appetite for the enigmatic, the esoteric, and
  the extraordinary."

  Friday, October 31, 2008

  Tired Of Givin' It Away
  By Billy Cox
  Published: Friday, October 31, 2008 at 3:02 p.m.
  Last Modified: Friday, October 31, 2008 at 3:18 p.m.
  "I'm sorry to be so agitated," says Peter Davenport from
  Harrington, Wash. "I'm at the end of my rope. With the
  government, with the press, with the American people. You've
  caught me at a strange time."
  This week, on his National UFO Reporting Center Web page, the man
  who runs one of the world's busiest eyewitness databases
  announced he was on the brink of shutting down his live telephone
  Hotline.
  "Typically," he wrote at http://www.nuforc.org/, "between 20 and
  80 percent of the calls we receive on any given day, I estimate,
  are prank calls, many of them grossly obscene and abusive. This
  rude behavior on the part of callers has had a significant, and
  adverse, effect on my desire to continue running NUFORC in the
  manner that we have done it in the past."
  But Davenport wasn't just torqued about idiot kids clogging his
  line with garbage. It was also about the inability of many
  eyewitnesses to follow basic instructions when filing their
  reports online or =97 for those who do figure it out =97 their horrid
  grammar, spelling and coherence.
  NUFORC has received roughly 25 calls a day, 24/7, since Davenport
  began running the show in 1994. With no salary. Plus minimum
  monthly expenses of $500, drawing largely upon the dwindling
  fortune he acquired by selling biotech stock from a business he
  founded.
  And then you've got all the leeches and parasites from the, ahem,
  MSM.
  "So you're asking me for information you can put on your blog,
  which you get paid for," Davenport tells De Void. "You know, I
  get calls like these all the time, from journalists who want to
  write articles, or radio shows that say, =91Come on our show for
  free. For free!'"
  It's thankless work. No wonder the Air Force quit the public gig
  in =9169. At least they got paid.
  "What's wrong with the American people? They've become a bunch of
  lazy do-nothings," Davenport goes on. "They call and tell me what


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/nov/m07-002.shtml[12/12/2011 09:35:36]
Tired Of Givin' It Away

  they saw, and I ask, look, can you write all this down and file a
  report? They say no. No =97 they can't take five minutes to write a
  report, but they have enough time to tell me about it."
  Americans. Sheesh.
  "I've been to 40 countries and I've never encountered less common
  sense that I find in this country. Americans pay king's ransoms
  to send their kids to school and all they learn is how to put on
  cheerleader outfits or football uniforms."
  Davenport takes a whack at all the preening egos using UFOs to
  peddle snake oil. He rattles off a list of con artists De Void
  recognizes. He says, "Ninety percent of the people in this field
  are charlatans."
  Then he cuts it short. "I've sort of rounded the corner with
  UFOlogy," he says. "I'm fed up with doing this for free."
  De Void recognizes UFO fatigue when he sees it. But Davenport's
  current dilemma was probably forged some 54 years ago, at age 6.
  That's when he saw a UFO hover and zip away near a drive-in movie
  outside St. Louis. Maybe the real curse here isn't the fatigue,
  but the perpetual second wind embodied by hobos in a Beckett
  farce.
  Estragon: "I can't go on like this."
  Vladimir: "That's what you think."

                                                          UFO Updates

                                               'Its All Here In Black & White'
    Location: UFOUpDatesList.Com > 2008 > Nov > Nov 7

                                             Mars Phoenix Probe in 'Hospice' Mode
  From: UFO UpDates - Toronto <ufoupdates.nul>
  Date: Fri, 07 Nov 2008 06:58:45 -0500
  Archived: Fri, 07 Nov 2008 06:58:45 -0500
  Subject: Mars Phoenix Probe in 'Hospice' Mode



  Source: The Discovery Channel - Silver Spring, Maryland, USA
  http://dsc.discovery.com/news/2008/11/05/mars-phoenix-hospice.html
  Nov. 5, 2008

  Mars Phoenix Probe in 'Hospice' Mode
  Irene Klotz, Discovery News
  Compared to NASA's long-lived Mars rovers, still scurrying around
  the red planet five years past warranty, the ice-sampling Phoenix
  lander, now in a communications coma five months after touchdown,
  may appear to be a bit of a dud.
  But there is nothing engineers could have done to fix the
  fundamental problem. Phoenix, which is stationed near the
  planet's northern pole, is running out of sunlight, a death knell
  for a solar-powered probe.
  When Phoenix landed on May 25, it was the start of summer on the
  Martian arctic circle, land of the midnight sun.
  The probe worked well enough for NASA to extend its planned 90-
  day mission until the end of the September, and later to mid-
  November. But with summer slipping into autumn and the sun
  dipping below the horizon for longer and longer periods of time,
  Phoenix has been struggling to generate enough power from its
  solar cells to keep functioning. It is dark now for more than
  seven hours a day.
  "We're in hospice mode," Phoenix principal investigator Peter
  Smith, with the University of Arizona in Tucson, told Discovery
  News.
  At best, NASA hopes to eke out a week's more monitoring of the
  changing conditions on Mars. The probe, whose prime mission was
  to chemically analyze ice and soil samples so scientists can
  determine if Mars was ever suitable to host life, is also
  equipped with meteorological instruments and cameras.
  There will be no more data coming back from Phoenix's miniature
  ovens and wet chemistry sets, which were used to assess ice and
  soil near the landing site.
  "We have all the data we're going to get," Smith said.
  Analysis is underway, and Smith said the team's goal is to
  announce results at a scientific meeting in December.
  "We didn't get every single thing we could have because of the
  complexity of delivering soil up there into the chambers," Smith
  added.
  The Martian soil turned out to be unexpectedly clumpy so that it
  clogged filters and complicated efforts to place samples into
  Phoenix's science chambers for processing.


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/nov/m07-004.shtml[12/12/2011 09:35:37]
Mars Phoenix Probe in 'Hospice' Mode


  The impediments, however, did not compromise the goals of the
  mission.
  Smith said he's not yet ready to state if Mars was suited for
  life, but he added, "I think there is going to be enough data to
  make a final pronouncement."
  Some of the Phoenix team's finding already have been announced.
  They include:
  * Confirmation of water ice on the planet's surface. Water is
  considered to be a key ingredient for supporting life.
  * An alkaline, rather than acidic, soil. On Earth, the pH of
  soil is important. Food plants, for example, thrive in acidic or
  neutral soil. So do bacteria. The finding does not necessarily
  nix the chances for life on Mars. "Life is very adaptable and can
  exist in many extreme environments," said Phoenix deputy project
  scientist Deborah Bass, at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in
  Pasadena, Calif.
  * A lack of sulfur compounds, or sulfates, in the soils near
  the Phoenix landing site. The Mars rovers Spirit and Opportunity
  found sulfates around their landing sites on the planet's
  equatorial region.
  * Soil grains show signs of weathering and varying chemical
  compositions.
  * A chemical in the soil called perchlorate, which on Earth
  exists in places with very little rainfall. Scientists are trying
  to determine what effect perchlorates could have on the prospect
  for life on Mars.
  "It's been a very successful mission," Smith said.

                                                  UFO 'Evidence' Is Unconvincing
  From: UFO UpDates - Toronto <ufoupdates.nul>
  Date: Fri, 07 Nov 2008 08:02:00 -0500
  Archived: Fri, 07 Nov 2008 08:02:00 -0500
  Subject: UFO 'Evidence' Is Unconvincing



  Source: LoHud.Com - Lower Hudson, New York, USA
  http://tinyurl.com/5bdy5w
  November 6, 2008

  UFO 'Evidence' Is Unconvincing
  It is understandable that eyewitnesses to the Hudson Valley UFO
  sightings of 25 years ago would stick to their stories all these
  years (Oct. 31 story). It is very likely that their reports
  accurately reflected what they saw in the night skies back then.
  The crucial point is that what they perceived did not accurately
  reflect what was actually present in the night skies. It is well-
  known that at night, where there is relatively little information
  about what an object is, people's perceptions wildly exaggerate
  the detail in what they see. That is, they really perceive
  details that are not really there.
  In dozens of so-called UFO sightings, it has turned out that
  credible witnesses perceived and reported much more detail than
  was present. These details made the perception much larger and
  more like a flying saucer than the object that was perceived -
   often just the lights of an aircraft at night. Eyewitness
  reports of flying saucers are totally unconvincing evidence for
  the reality of such things. The actual cause of the Hudson Valley
  UFO sightings was a group of private pilots who got up to hoaxing
  by flying around in the night sky turning their aircraft lights
  on and off. There is a complete lack of credible photographic or
  physical evidence (but lots of fakes, hoaxes and well-intentioned
  photos of little lights on a dark background) for flying saucers.
  Visitors from outer space are not whizzing around Earth looking
  to do mischief, bring us peace and love, or better recipes for
  lasagna.

  Terence Hines

  [Thanks to Greg Boone for the lead]

                                          Witness Recounts UFO Crash Near Roswell
  From: UFO UpDates - Toronto <ufoupdates.nul>
  Date: Fri, 07 Nov 2008 11:02:27 -0500
  Archived: Fri, 07 Nov 2008 11:02:27 -0500
  Subject: Witness Recounts UFO Crash Near Roswell



  Source: Frank Warren's The UFO Chronicles Blog
  http://tinyurl.com/68ahl5
  11-5-08

  Thursday, November 06, 2008
  My UFO Experience: Witness Recounts The Night A UFO Crashed Near
  Roswell, New Mexico
  Reader Submitted Report
  I am a 70 year old retired psychotherapist. I grew up in Santa
  Rosa, New Mexico, which is around 90 miles or less north from
  Roswell, New Mexico, where the UFO's crashed. I was 9 years old
  on that 7/47 night in question I vividly remember around 10:30 pm
  or so, looking into the sky and seeing a V-shaped line of about
  eleven lights streaking across the sky, first from one area, then
  from another, then another. They were streaking across the sky at
  a rate of speed that was quite clearly faster than anything made
  on earth in 1947. After about five minutes the V-shape changed to
  a diagonal line and continued the same pattern of streaking
  across the clear sky for a few more minutes.
  Needless to say I was stunned. In the morning I dashed down the
  street to tell Mr. Hoy what I had seen. He was the editor of the
  small newspaper, put out once a week. He shared with me that the
  Deputy Sheriff, Joe Pat Downing, was on patrol the night before
  and had told him he had seen the same thing.
  The vividness of that memory has stayed with me and it wasn't
  until thirty years later that I started hearing about the UFO
  crash in Roswell. That was when I connected my experience that
  night seeing those strange lights with what was taking place 90
  miles south of my hometown. It is also my understanding that
  "weather balloons" don't do that....

  continuity of effort Davenport via NUFORC has been able to
  establish will, over time, be dissipated and dispersed to less
  organized or coherent venues.
  On the other hand, this may also present an opportunity to change
  and rethink the problem of how difficult and inefficient a manner
  of gathering reliable reports and data on contemporaneous ufo
  sightings has increasingly been for NUFORC, and consider more
  practical means of better collecting and filtering such reports,
  and even more importantly, providing legit researchers more of an
  ability and avenue to further, more practically investigate


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/nov/m07-009.shtml[12/12/2011 09:35:39]
Re: Tired Of Givin' It Away

  serious and significant reports than NUFORC is either capable or
  willing to provide currently.
  For example, one of NUFORC's long-standing problems and
  deficiencies, imho, and based on analytical observation, has been
  that, while brief synopses of reports are collected on his
  website database, the comprehensive details and raw data of
  collected reports have been quite restricted by and who Davenport
  thinks should be involved in further investigation of same. I
  don't believe he has a very good system of providing access to or
  computerized tools for analyzing the data patterns within the
  reports he has collected over the past couple decades, but being
  almost completely a one-man operation, with inadequate, self-
   funded support, who can blame him?
  His main problem, at the moment, is how better to screen out the
  bogus, and nastily prankish calls of "reports" NUFORC has been
  receiving, and perhaps an automated telephone response, involving
  a recording, should be used, indicating caller ID or other
  identification trace-back tech, should be used and to notify
  callers that only serious reports are accepted. Of course, that
  might make the idiots even more motivated to prank or hack such a
  system, so it's quite a dilemma.
  He may have to resort to not taking direct calls in real time,
  and be reduced to only recording or taking of such reports (as
  are legit) to witnesses filing reports even more than now by
  filling out the report form he maintains on his website. Still,
  the process of appropriate, effective filtration will remain
  there, also.
  Perhaps a "caller ID" or "warning" recording that requires a
  call-back number, and/or taking reports by message machine or
  voicemail intially, and a time-delayed review by a person who
  listens to initial reports called in to determine if follow-up is
  needed. Problem there is, however, the same as noted in the
  article - how do you reduce or screen out the idiot calls, or
  separate the wheat from the nasty chaff, and also without
  reducing the efforts of legit reporters from either wanting or
  being able to make their own reports? I really don't know how you
  do this on a limited budget with relatively few people.
  Anyone got any better ideas about how NUFORC might handle this
  problem?

  Steve

UK Black Boxes To 'Collect Every Email'

                                   A mailing list for the study of UFO-related phenomena
                                               'Its All Here In Black & White'
    Location: UFOUpDatesList.Com > 2008 > Nov > Nov 7

                                           UK Black Boxes To 'Collect Every Email'
  From: UFO UpDates - Toronto <ufoupdates.nul>
  Date: Fri, 07 Nov 2008 12:17:00 -0500
  Archived: Fri, 07 Nov 2008 12:17:00 -0500
  Subject: UK Black Boxes To 'Collect Every Email'



  Source: The Independent - London, England, UK
  http://tinyurl.com/6q8dfv
  Wednesday, 5 November 2008

  Government Black Boxes Will 'Collect Every Email'
  Home Office says all data from web could be stored in giant
  government database
  By Robert Verkaik, Law Editor
  Internet "black boxes" will be used to collect every email and
  web visit in the UK under the Government's plans for a giant "big
  brother" database, The Independent has learnt.
  Home Office officials have told senior figures from the internet
  and telecommunications industries that the "black box" technology
  could automatically retain and store raw data from the web before
  transferring it to a giant central database controlled by the
  Government.
  Plans to create a database holding information about every phone
  call, email and internet visit made in the UK have provoked a
  huge public outcry. Richard Thomas, the Information Commissioner,
  described it as "step too far" and the Government's own terrorism
  watchdog said that as a "raw idea" it was "awful".
  Nevertheless, ministers have said they are committed to
  consulting on the new Communications Data Bill early in the new
  year. News that the Government is already preparing the ground by
  trying to allay the concerns of the internet industry is bound to
  raise suspicions about ministers' true intentions. Further
  details of the database emerged on Monday at a meeting of
  internet service providers (ISPs) in London where representatives
  from BT, AOL Europe, O2 and BSkyB were given a PowerPoint
  presentation of the issues and the technology surrounding the
  Government's Interception Modernisation Programme (IMP), the name
  given by the Home Office to the database proposal.
  Whitehall experts working on the IMP unit told the meeting the
  security and intelligence agencies wanted to use the stored data
  to help fight serious crime and terrorism, and said the
  technology would allow them to create greater "capacity" to
  monitor all communication traffic on the internet. The "black
  boxes" are an attractive option for the internet industry because
  they would be secure and not require any direct input from the
  ISPs.
  During the meeting Whitehall officials also tried to reassure the
  industry by suggesting that many smaller ISPs would be unaffected
  by the "black boxes" as these would be installed upstream on the
  network and hinted that all costs would be met by the Government.
  "It was clear the 'black box' is the technology the Government


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/nov/m07-011.shtml[12/12/2011 09:35:40]
UK Black Boxes To 'Collect Every Email'

  will use to hold all the data. But what isn't clear is what the
  Home Secretary, GCHQ and the security services intend to do with
  all this information in the future," said a source close to the
  meeting.
  He added: "They said they only wanted to return to a position
  they were in before the emergence of internet communication, when
  they were able to monitor all correspondence with a police
  suspect. The difference here is they will be in a much better
  position to spy on many more people on the basis of their
  internet behaviour. Also there's a grey area between what is
  content and what is traffic. Is what is said in a chat room
  content or just traffic?"
  Ministers say plans for the database have not been confirmed, and
  that it is not their intention to introduce monitoring or storage
  equipment that will check or hold the content of emails or
  phonecalls on the traffic.
  A spokesman for the Home Office said that Monday's meeting
  provided a "chance to engage with small communication service
  providers" ahead of the formal public consultation next year. He
  added: "We need to work closely with the internet service
  providers and the communication service providers. The meeting
  was to show the top-line challenges faced in the future. We are
  public about the IMP, but we are still working out the detail.
  There will a consultation on the Communications Data Bill early
  next year."
  A spokesman for the Internet Service Providers Association said
  the organisation was pleased the Home Office had addressed its
  members and was keen to continue dialogue while awaiting a formal
  consultation.
  Database plans were first announced by the Prime Minister in
  February. It is not clear where the records will be held but GCHQ
  may eventually be the project's home.

  [Thanks to 'The Norm' for the lead]

  While I've never seen a UFO, and haven't tried to shoot any kind
  of craft in the sky, I've enjoyed taking stereoscopic pictures
  over the years. First it was stereo slides with an old Stereo
  Realist from the fifties, now held together with duct tape. You'd
  need to do special mounting of the half-frame slides. Now I use a
  Loreo, which can be processed at any consumer photo processing
  place, both images printing onto a standard 4x6" print. Don't
  know if it would be any good for night-time shots, probably
  wouldn't be good for much of a distance. I've not tried using a
  diffraction grating. While the consumer-level 3D camera devices
  are going to provide documentation of a UFO at the level we'd
  like, they may provide some information that would be missing
  from single lens photos.
  I see that Loreo now make a "3D Lens-In-A-Cap." The blurb on it
  says,
  "Not since the mid-1960s has there been an affordable and easy
  way to take 3D stereo images with your regular 2D camera. Now
  there is 3D Lens-In-A-Cap, the stereo beam-split attachment that
  fits right in place of your standard lens on your camera. " It
  can be mounted on your camera in mid-roll if needed, as it
  replaces your usual lens.
  The basic Loreo and the 3D Lens in a Cap attachment (versions are
  available for most of the major camera brands) are around $100
  each. Might be worth having around if you are in an area with


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/nov/m07-012.shtml[12/12/2011 09:35:41]
Re: The Triumph Of Ostriches

  ongoing sightings.
  Around the same price is a rather ingenious mechanism to take
  stereoscopic images with any consumer digital camera that has a
  standard tripod mounting socket on the bottom. You attach the
  Photo3-D attachment (about the size of a cell phone) to the
  bottom of your camera, snap one frame, and the slide the camera
  over to the other end to take the other frame to get the proper
  separation. With its PC or Mac software, you can print out images
  on your own printer.
  If you are caught without a proper stereo camera, David Lee
  describes the freehand technique called the "Astronaut shuffle"
  (AKA the "Side-step" or "Cha-cha"). This would not be useful for
  moving objects, however. The aim is to get the two shots taken
  from positions that are the equivalent of the separation between
  your own two pupils.
  "If you're not sure if you want to get into stereo photography,
  but want to see if you can make a stereo image, the easiest way
  is to use your regular camera and take two photographs using the
  side- step method (also known as the astronaut shuffle because
  the astronauts used this method on the moon to make stereo images
  with a Hasselblad). All you have to do is compose the image in
  your viewfinder, then shift your weight onto your left foot and
  make the first exposure, then shift your weight over to your
  right foot and make the second exposure."
  Some stereoscopy resources:
  http://www.3dstereo.com/viewmaster/sca-lic.html
  http://www.photo3-d.com/?stereo
  http://www.stereoscopy.com/

  bright UFO, but a very bright near point-source UFO, and a steady
  long exposure too (but they were hand-held!) in order to get a
  useful spectrum.
  It's hard to believe this programme was ever a serious one
  really.

Mystery Deepens Over Unseen Antarctic 'Alps'




                                                          UFO Updates
                                   A mailing list for the study of UFO-related phenomena
                                               'Its All Here In Black & White'
    Location: UFOUpDatesList.Com > 2008 > Nov > Nov 7

                                       Mystery Deepens Over Unseen Antarctic 'Alps'
  From: UFO UpDates - Toronto <ufoupdates.nul>
  Date: Fri, 07 Nov 2008 16:38:53 -0500
  Archived: Fri, 07 Nov 2008 16:38:53 -0500
  Subject: Mystery Deepens Over Unseen Antarctic 'Alps'



  Source: National Geograpic - Washington, DC, USA
  http://tinyurl.com/5nhk6s
  November 6, 2008

  Mystery Deepens Over Unseen Antarctic 'Alps'
  Rebecca Carroll
  for National Geographic News
  The existence of a massive Antarctic mountain range buried under
  miles of ice has become an even deeper mystery, a new study says.
  The little-researched Gamburtsev Mountains seem to challenge
  geologic patterns seen in other mountain ranges on Earth.
  For one, the range is situated in the middle of the continent
  instead of on the edge=97at the plate-tectonic boundaries=97like most
  other mountains. See a high-resolution map of Antarctica:
  http://tinyurl.com/2eq4sr
  The range's high peaks reach an elevation of about 10,000 feet
  (more than 3,000 meters)=97heights typical of relatively young
  mountain ranges, such as the spiky Rockies and the European Alps.
  New findings based on river sediments, which suggest the range is
  more than 500 million years old, are intriguing, experts say.
  Older mountains, such as the Appalachian range in the eastern
  U.S., are thought to be shorter and less rugged after hundreds of
  millions of years of erosion.
  Because the Gamburtsev range is tall, some scientists have argued
  it must have formed relatively recently=97within the last 60
  million years or so.
  And because it's not near a tectonic boundary, some have
  suggested the range rose up as the result of magma buildup around
  a theoretical volcanic hot spot.
  (Related: "Under-Ice Volcano Eruption Spewed Ash Over Antarctica"
  [January 21, 2008].)
  "The hypothesis that the mountains are derived from young
  volcanic activity is hard to reconcile with our data," said study
  lead author Tina van de Flierdt of the Imperial College London.
  Hard to Reconcile
  Scientists examined sediments collected from a coastal area that
  would have been a vast delta about 35 million years ago, when
  Antarctica's rivers carried flowing water instead of glacier ice.
  If the mountains were made of relatively recent volcanic
  material, some of it should have been in the sediment as


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/nov/m07-015.shtml[12/12/2011 09:35:42]
Mystery Deepens Over Unseen Antarctic 'Alps'

  Gamburtsev runoff passed through the delta.
  Instead, all mineral grains the researchers dated=97such as zircon
  and hornblende=97were more than 500 million years old.
  "Volcanic activity of the extent to form a mountain range bigger
  than the European Alps would leave a 'geochemical fingerprint' in
  the preglacial to present-day sediments=97we simply can't see this
  fingerprint," van de Flierdt said.
  The study, which is based in part on van de Flierdt's work at
  Columbia University, was published online this week by
  Geophysical Research Letters.
  Missing Erosion
  A remaining mystery, according to study co-author Sidney Hemming,
  is why the mountains have not eroded more.
  "The new data we're collecting makes it look like the erosion
  rates are so extremely low," said the Columbia University
  geochemist.
  Hemming cautioned that researchers can't be certain the sediments
  are from the mountain.
  It's possible, she added, that the ice has helped keep the rocks
  in place, but that does not explain the lack of erosion from
  ancient periods when the ice was not there.
  "We can say that they're either not hot spot volcanic [mountains]
  or that they formed after the ice basically capped them off,"
  Hemming said.
  But, she said, later formation is highly unlikely: "It would be
  hard to imagine that it wouldn't leave some evidence in the ice
  or sediments."
  Not Volcanic
  The study makes a good case for the theory that the mountains
  were not formed by recent volcanic activity, said University of
  Arizona geochemist Peter Reiners, who was not involved with the
  research.
  "If the mountains themselves are anywhere close to the same age
  as the rocks, then the Gamburtsevs are trying to tell us
  something about how really old topography can persist for
  hundreds of millions of years without being worn down by water,
  wind, and glaciers," said Reiners, who also studies the range.
  Norm Sleep, a Stanford University geophysicist who also studies
  the Gamburtsev Mountains but wasn't involved with this study,
  agreed with the data but not the interpretation.
  Sleep worried that "550-million-year-old highlands would have
  long since eroded away."
  Instead, he suggests a gooey, semi-solid plume of material could
  have formed a pond deep under Earth's cooler outer lid of rock.
  This would have caused the mountains to rise without spewing
  magma all over the surface.
  Such an event may have happened within the last 50 million years,
  he said.

  >"If you're not sure if you want to get into stereo photography,
  >but want to see if you can make a stereo image, the easiest way
  >is to use your regular camera and take two photographs using the

  never realizing that it had such a cute name. Some samples made
  using this simple method may be seen at

  achieved with an inexpensive camera and software to make one
  image out of the left and right views. I use an antique stereo
  viewer picked up at a flea market to view the pictures right on
  the computer screen.
  So the next time you see a UFO hanging motionless overhead, take
  two pictures instead of one.

  The dance is pretty simple. A bold expression of surprise with
  hands up near the face. The hands move to mime taking a photo. On
  the rimshot you move your right index finger to click, shift
  your weight over to the other leg with a fetching wiggle of your
  booty, and click on the next rim shot. More wiggling of booty, of
  course.

  with Hasselblad optional). You see the UFO, you whip out your

  include instructions on showing part of the landscape so the UFO

  stereo images from multiple angles... See if we can get the

  song, "Is That You Mo-dean?"

  gazillion hits. Once you've done your successful meme farming,
  next time a UFO appears over a crowd of people, they won't gawp
  like they just fell off the turnip truck. Someone will whistle
  the first few bars, and everybody will pull out their cameras and
  does the Astronaut Shuffle, just like the video programmed them
  to. Data galore.

  the Astronaut Shuffle. No-one can see you experiment with shaking
  your booty for science. As Pasteur said, chance favors the
  prepared mind.

  Archived: Mon, 10 Nov 2008 06:49:26 -0500
  Subject: E-Mail Flowing Again



  The problem was that there were 73,000 spams that had piled
  up in the /mail/temp/ folder on the VSN server since October 20th.
  Where in past years un-wanted mail was seemingly discarded, the
  'rules' have once again changed. The spam in that folder caused

  a VSN e-mail address and password. It was only concentrated
  digging on my part that eventually revealled the source of the
  problem and the system corrected itself late yesterday.
  The board of directors and our huge staff are contemplating
  future options but consensus is difficult to reach and with
  the current world-wide economic situation may take an hour
  or two...
  Meanwhile, List-mail should return to normal.

  >It is understandable that eyewitnesses to the Hudson Valley UFO
  >sightings of 25 years ago would stick to their stories all these
  >years (Oct. 31 story). It is very likely that their reports
  >accurately reflected what they saw in the night skies back then.
  >The crucial point is that what they perceived did not accurately
  >reflect what was actually present in the night skies. It is well-
  >known that at night, where there is relatively little information
  >about what an object is, people's perceptions wildly exaggerate
  >the detail in what they see. That is, they really perceive
  >details that are not really there.
  >In dozens of so-called UFO sightings, it has turned out that
  >credible witnesses perceived and reported much more detail than
  >was present. These details made the perception much larger and
  >more like a flying saucer than the object that was perceived -
  > often just the lights of an aircraft at night. Eyewitness
  >reports of flying saucers are totally unconvincing evidence for
  >the reality of such things. The actual cause of the Hudson Valley
  >UFO sightings was a group of private pilots who got up to hoaxing
  >by flying around in the night sky turning their aircraft lights
  >on and off. There is a complete lack of credible photographic or
  >physical evidence (but lots of fakes, hoaxes and well-intentioned
  >photos of little lights on a dark background) for flying saucers.
  >Visitors from outer space are not whizzing around Earth looking
  >to do mischief, bring us peace and love, or better recipes for
  >lasagna.
  >Terence Hines
  This blog is simple minded and unconvincing.
  Don Ledger

  The Huddersfield Daily Examiner in West Yorkshire, UK reports

  was walking along Smithy Lane in Skelmanthorpe last Friday
  around 7pm, when they saw a strange orange light in the sky.
  The father, Anndy Evans, said that the silent object flew "about
  the speed of a plane" but it stopped "like a helicopter". Mrs.
  Evans thought it was on fire and the daughter, Amber, age five,
  thought it was a spaceship.

  hovered.
  There have been a string of mysterious incidents in the skies
  above Huddersfield since July.
  Earlier this month Deighton woman Tracey Britton spotted strange
  orange lights in the sky while walking near Huddersfield Broad
  canal.
  In August four people said they saw a bright white light above
  Huddersfield. They also reported hearing a loud Tardis-like
  noise.
  In July people in the Holme Valley reported seeing strange red
  lights in the sky, but after an appeal in the Examiner it turned
  out the mysterious lights were nothing more mysterious than
  fast-flying Chinese lanterns.
  A Discovery Channel series episode of Investigation X is
  called "UFO Outbreak," aired in mid October. According to
  Aircraft Maintenance Technology, the hour-long episode is a
  "forensic investigation of the mass UFO sightings" earlier this
  year in Stephenville, TX; Kokomo, IN; and Southwick, MA.
  American Chronicle reports that on Oct. 4 UFOs were sighted
  hovering near a Bruce Springsteen concert in Philadelphia. The
  story was broadcast on WPVI-TV, Channel 6 (ABC affiliate), on
  Oct. 8.

                                    Re: Universe Might Be Bigger Older And Stranger
  From: Martin Shough <parcellular.nul>
  Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2008 15:29:25 -0000
  Archived: Mon, 10 Nov 2008 10:52:38 -0500
  Subject: Re: Universe Might Be Bigger Older And Stranger

  >From: Ray Dickenson <r.dickenson.nul>
  >To: <ufoupdates.nul>

  >Subject: Universe Might Be Bigger Older And Stranger Place
  >Hello List
  >Here are two recent news items:
  >http://tinyurl.com/6frtmw
  >Professor Brian Cox (particle physics, Manchester University)
  >on the unanswered questions - quote begins "the wheels are
  >starting to come off our picture of reality" quote ends.
  Gosh. This sounds like some cataclysm coming out of nowhere to
  knock those complacent scientists off their pedestal. I can't
  say that creating this impression was actually your intention,
  but it would be consistent with your usual style.
  In fact Cox says "... in a sense, I feel the wheels are starting
  to come off our picture of reality. This is why the Large Hadron
  Collider is being built." He is not saying anything different
  here from what the entire community of physicists has agreed
  upon with increasing focus and frustration over the course of
  several decades.
  There are deep unresolved mysteries in the standard model of
  particle physics. Not news. Far from suppressing this fact most
  physicists have been earning their mortgage repayments by
  probing at them at them in some fashion all their professional
  lives. Nothing would please any of them more than earning a
  Nobel or two for finding "the answers". Some of the problems
  they've worried at have generated a range of possible
  theoretical resolutions that can hopefully be tested by going to
  LHC energies. Possibly (almost certainly, on some level) there
  will be completely new physics revealed too, which will beckon
  theorists towards another layer of the explanatory onion. All
  very exciting. But how do you imagine those problems came to put
  such pressure on the standard model in the first place? They
  were discovered by physicists in the course of trying to make it
  work. It's physicists who yank the wheels off their old models
  of reality, in order that physicists can make new ones.
  >http://tinyurl.com/5gyx49
  >On dark flow - quote begins "this motion is caused by structures
  >well beyond the current cosmological horizon, which is more than
  >14 billion light-years away" quote ends
  >Just that last item implies the real universe can be ten times,
  >or hundred or thousands of times bigger, and therefore older,
  >than we thought.
  This is a misunderstanding. Imagine yourself as an observer at a
  point on that 14 BLY light horizon: You still have a light
  horizon forming a sphere all around you at 14 BLY. Every
  observer at any point in spacetime is the centre of such an
  horizon, but not every observer is causally connected with all


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/nov/m10-009.shtml[12/12/2011 09:35:51]
Re: Universe Might Be Bigger Older And Stranger

  of the points encompassed by every other observer's horizon. It
  has never been part of the standard cosmological model (SCM) to
  say that there is no more cosmos beyond our light horizon. This
  is just the observable universe (often just called "the
  universe" for simplicity). There could be many times the mass of
  known galaxies beyond the light horizon - or there could even be
  less, it all depends on the large scale geometry of spacetime.
  The 14 BLY is (in some sense) the _age_ of light that might
  reach us from this surface (if the last scattering surface were
  not in the way) but it is not the spacetime radius of the
  universe, which in the expanding curved space of the SCM is
  _much_ larger by a Hubble scale factor, and would contain many
  overlapping horizons (which has to do with the "horizon problem"
  leading to inflation theories of course). Nevertheless, the age
  of the universe as measured by the light horizon is the same 14
  BLY "Hubble radius" for observers everywhere. So this discovery
  doesn't make the universe "older than we thought".
  The article doesn't give any idea of why discovering evidence of
  mass hot-spots beyond our light horizon should "rewrite the laws
  of physics" or "explode physics as we know it". This is garbage
  journalism. The novelty of the new observation (if it and its
  interpretation both hold up, which may well not happen as they
  often don't) is that it suggests the larger scale structure of
  the cosmos beyond the light horizon is not homogeneous, i.e. it
  might still have lumps in it. This would be fantastically
  interesting and strikes a chord with my prejudices, because
  whilst the SCM presupposes there is a 'homogeneity scale' at
  which the cosmos can be modelled as though it were a smooth
  fluid (because only in this case can General Relativity be used
  to model it using the usual simplified FLRW type metric) there
  has long been a minority view that galaxy surveys indicate a
  fractal structure, which _could_ imply new physics beyond GR.
  >So we could be looking at evolution (and migration, and
  >advancement) opportunities stretching back trillions of years,
  >compared to our Earth life's evolution of 3 or 4 billion, and
  >our human technology of perhaps two hundred years.
  See above.
  >Taken with the first item, and with John D Barrow's forecast, in
  >The Constants of Nature, that "eventually, our current theories
  >will all be shown to be wrong", it seems we're just peeking over
  >the back-yard fence, as far as knowledge is concerned.
  I'm sure that's right. It's a basic tenet of the
  philosophy/sociology of science - and, again, has been for many
  decades - that the current theory paradigm of every age is
  destined to live on only as a limit case subsumed inside a
  future theory with broader application (which is what "wrong"
  means). And that appliies to today as much as it did to
  Newtonian physics. Glad that you and the physicists agree. It's
  just a shame that there is no short cut to finding out what's in
  the future. They just have to go there!

  Martin Shough

  >To: <ufoupdates.nul>

  >There are deep unresolved mysteries in the standard model of
  >particle physics. Not news. Far from suppressing this fact most
  >physicists have been earning their mortgage repayments by
  >probing at them at them in some fashion all their professional
  >lives.
  An element of understatement there.
  String theorists have practically industrialised the process of
  multiplying the number of unresolved mysteries.
  And in all of this there is an ever-widening epistemological
  gap: as the problem of describing how it all works becomes more
  difficult and complex, so we get further and further away from
  even addressing the issue of why it all works that way.
  I suspect that somewhere deep in our collective psyche there is
  a myth to which we adhere: that of the 'clockwork model', a
  closed, discrete system called the universe, capable of being
  laid bare to the human understanding by a sufficiently complete
  description of its parts and the laws governing their
  interactions. Every time a piece of information or academic
  conjecture that challenges this myth seeps into the arena of
  public discourse there is a consequent mini-shockwave of
  confused reaction: the media pokes a bit of fun at the
  physicists; fringe theorists renew their licence to engage in
  unwarranted conjecture, each according to their respective hobby
  horses; the public at large becomes a little more ignorant as to
  the real nature of our collective scientific ignorance.
  The cycle is as dispiriting as it is tedious.
  For my own part I have nothing but admiration for those
  theoretical physicists who grapple with the frontier of our
  understanding. It's hard, mindbending work out there at the
  edge!
  --
  Gerald O'Connell

Phoenix Lander Finishes Work On Red Planet
